item.title: ISO 5230, 18974, and 42001 Comparison
item.description:
1. Relationship Among the Three Standards

A company that develops AI systems using open source stands at the point where three standards intersect.

flowchart LR
 subgraph oss["Open source management"]
 A["ISO/IEC 5230\nLicense compliance\n(licenses, SBOM, artifacts)"]
 B["ISO/IEC 18974\nSecurity assurance\n(vulnerability detection, response, CVD)"]
 end

 subgraph ai["AI system management"]
 C["ISO/IEC 42001\nAI management system\n(governance, risk, life cycle)"]
 end

 oss -- "Open source compliance\nwithin AI systems" --> ai

ISO 5230 and 18974 are standards for managing open source itself, while ISO 42001 is a standard for managing AI systems. The two areas are independent, but they intersect when AI systems use open source.

item.title: ISO/IEC 5230 vs 18974 Comparison
item.description:
1. Relationship Between the Two Standards

ISO/IEC 5230 and ISO/IEC 18974 are both international open source standards led by the OpenChain Project, but they address different problems. 5230 covers open source license compliance (fulfillment of copyright obligations, SBOM management, and distribution of Compliance Artifacts), while 18974 covers open source security assurance (vulnerability detection, assessment, response, and CVD). The two standards do not have a complete superset/subset relationship. They share 9 common clauses covering policy, competence, SBOM, and similar areas, but each has its own exclusive clauses — 5230 has clauses for license compliance, artifacts, and contributions, while 18974 has clauses for Standard Practice Implementation and Security Assurance.
